title: New Document Source Entry Delivery
summary: add a management-only New action to configured sub-scope report lists and open every interactively created document in Source mode
content_html:
New Document Source Entry Delivery

Result

A configured docs_subscope report has a management-only New button on its list toolbar. The action creates one document in that report's exact { scope, sub_scope } collection, routes the report to the new document, and immediately opens the existing Source editor with the returned { scope, sub_scope, doc_id } target.

The ordinary scope-level New, New Child, and New Sibling actions adopt the same post-create rule: after a successful create and projection refresh, open the new document in Source mode.

The generated heading remains the committed starting source, but the user does not have to perform a second action before writing useful content.

This extends the exact-target editor delivered by Manage Sub-Scope Documents and the management contribution boundary maintained by Sub-Scope Index. It remains a generic Docs Viewer capability rather than Tag Registry behavior.

Starting Gap

  • At the start of this delivery, POST /docs/create created only a parent-scope document.
  • The existing scope-level New actions create, refresh the main index, select the new document, and leave it in rendered mode.
  • The source editor already accepts one exact parent or configured sub-scope target and freezes that target for the mounted session.
  • The manage-only sub-scope report contribution already owns list-toolbar controls, but its current controls are selection-backed actions. It has no collection-level New action.

The new report action therefore needs a bounded sub-scope create seam. Opening Source after the create should be one shared interactive post-create behavior, not a report-specific imitation of source entry.

User Contract

Report New

  • New appears as a compact 📄 icon button only in the local management report list, with New retained as its accessible label. Public reports retain no create control and import no management module.
  • The button is a collection action. It uses the mounted report's validated { scope, sub_scope }; it never derives a destination from a checked row, displayed detail, selected parent, URL text, or tag registry record.
  • New remains available for an empty collection and is independent of checkbox-selection mode and selection-backed Actions.
  • The action opens the existing title modal with the New heading, ordinary New-document defaults, and a compact label row that gives the title input more width. Cancel creates nothing.
  • Confirm creates one new flat sub-scope document. Sub-scope documents do not accept parent_id.
  • After the commit, the manage inventory refreshes, the canonical report route becomes ?doc=<report-doc-id>&subdoc=<new-doc-id>, and Source opens with the exact returned child target.
  • Save/Rebuild and Return to doc return to that new document's rendered report detail without changing the parent report selection.

Shared Post-Create Source Entry

The interactive document-creation rule is:

create
  -> receive exact committed target
  -> refresh the owning projection
  -> establish the new rendered route/selection
  -> open Source with that exact target

It applies to:

  • the new sub-scope report New action;
  • the existing scope-level New action;
  • New Child; and
  • New Sibling.

For parent-scope actions the committed target is { scope, doc_id }. For the report action it is { scope, sub_scope, doc_id }.

Source mode remains local presentation state. It is not encoded as a URL parameter, and source entry does not weaken the existing fixed-target, dirty buffer, stale-revision, rebuild, or Return contracts.

Committed-Create Failure Boundary

Creation and post-create presentation are separate outcomes.

  • A create failure reports Create failed and does not enter Source.
  • If creation commits but refresh, routing, or Source mounting fails, the UI reports that the document was created but could not be opened in Source.
  • Recovery may retry refresh or source entry for the returned target. It must not retry document creation silently.
  • The created heading-only source remains a valid recoverable document.

Create Service Contract

The existing POST /docs/create mutation family accepts an optional sub_scope.

Parent request:

{ scope, title, optional parent_id }

Sub-scope request:

{ scope, sub_scope, title }

The service:

  • preserves the current parent behavior when sub_scope is absent;
  • requires a configured one-level child when sub_scope is present;
  • resolves and confines the configured child source-document root;
  • rejects parent_id for a sub-scope create;
  • allocates the immutable document identity within the destination collection and retains the atomic create-only collision boundary;
  • writes the standard source front matter and # <title> body;
  • preserves the existing scope creation default for viewable rather than introducing a report-specific publication policy;
  • runs the normal targeted sub-scope document projection without adding parent search membership;
  • returns the committed record plus an exact target; and
  • records the exact scope, optional sub_scope, doc_id, and source path in its activity result.

The create path does not read or validate the Tag Registry. New Tag bootstrap, registry compensation, and doc_url[] association remain separate owners.

Ownership

  • docs_management_mutations.py owns parent and optional sub-scope create planning. It reuses the configured managed-target/root rules rather than introducing an unconfined path lookup.
  • docs_management_mutation_service.py and the existing /docs/create route own write/rebuild execution and the committed response.
  • docs-viewer-management-subscope-contribution.js owns the management-only report-list button and passes the mounted collection identity outward.
  • docs-viewer-management-document-reports.js bridges that collection action to the local management create workflow and report refresh/navigation.
  • The shared sub-scope report continues to own list/detail navigation and subdoc route state. It does not become a source editor or mutation client.
  • docs-viewer-management-actions.js owns the reusable interactive create-to-Source transition used by existing parent creation actions.
  • docs-viewer-management.js and the existing source-mode service retain exact-target Source entry; no second editor or target resolver is added.

Boundary

In scope:

  • optional exact sub_scope support in the existing create mutation family;
  • one management-only, collection-level New report-list control;
  • creation in configured flat one-level sub-scopes;
  • refreshing the manage inventory and routing to the created subdoc;
  • opening the existing Source editor immediately after successful interactive creation;
  • applying that post-create rule to scope New, New Child, and New Sibling;
  • committed-create recovery that never duplicates the write; and
  • focused service, pure module, route, and manual UI evidence.

Not in scope:

  • public creation controls or public write-service access;
  • using the selected, displayed, checked, or URL document as an implicit creation target;
  • nested sub-scope documents or parent_id inside a flat sub-scope;
  • adding sub-scope documents to the parent Index, Recent, or global search;
  • changing viewable defaults or automatically publishing a new document;
  • entering Source after imports, transfers, package operations, migrations, New Tag bootstrap, or other non-interactive creation;
  • changing the source editor, Markdown/front-matter split, or metadata model;
  • adding title/source synchronization beyond existing metadata behavior; or
  • Tag Registry doc_url[], document picker, or semantic-token work.

Delivery Tracker

Current state: delivery complete. NDS-4 acceptance passed.

Review rule: complete one phase, record exact evidence, and stop for review before the next phase.

[x] NDS-0 — Freeze Target, UI, And Post-Commit Contracts

  • [x] Confirm that existing Source entry accepts exact parent and sub-scope targets and retains the target for the editor session.
  • [x] Confirm that current /docs/create is parent-only and existing New actions stop in rendered mode after reloading the parent index.
  • [x] Place report New in the management-only list contribution and keep it independent of selection so an empty collection can create its first document.
  • [x] Freeze the create, refresh, route, and Source-entry order.
  • [x] Freeze the committed-create recovery rule: retry presentation, never the create.
  • [x] Keep public reports, non-interactive creation, publication policy, and Tag Registry workflows outside this delivery.

Checkpoint / review gate: accepted design only; no runtime behavior changed.

[x] NDS-1 — Add Exact Sub-Scope Create Planning

  • [x] Extend the existing create planner and response with optional sub_scope and exact returned target.
  • [x] Resolve only a configured one-level child source root and reject parent_id, unknown children, nested targets, mismatched identities, and escaping paths.
  • [x] Preserve existing parent mutation behavior; the additive exact target is the only parent response extension.
  • [x] Reuse standard identity, front matter, viewability default, atomic create, targeted rebuild, and activity contracts.
  • [x] Add focused planner/service/route evidence for parent compatibility, valid child creation, empty child collection, collision, invalid collection, write failure, and rebuild failure.

NDS-1 implementation and evidence

  • plan_create now resolves an optional sub_scope through the configured managed-collection owner, validates every existing direct-child filename and front-matter identity, and writes the new source only beneath that resolved root. Child requests reject parent_id; child source and response records omit it.
  • Parent create responses retain their existing shape with one additive exact target. Child responses add sub_scope and return { scope, sub_scope, doc_id }. Both retain the parent scope's existing viewable default.
  • Create writes now use the existing atomic create-only writer. A destination appearing after planning is not overwritten. A write failure remains pre-commit; a rebuild failure returns an HTTP error payload containing the committed target, committed: true, and retry_create: false.
  • Focused pytest over create planning/routes, managed targets, metadata, sub-scope delete recovery, and write/rebuild execution: 84 passed. The route fixture created only temporary parent/child sources and intercepted the generated rebuild boundary; it did not create a repository document or wire any browser action.
  • Maintained explicit Python lint over the three changed service files and the focused create test: passed. Python compilation for the same four files: passed.
  • Studio docs/search dry-runs reported 230 documents, 13 tree roots, zero pending writes, and zero warnings. git diff --check: passed.

Checkpoint / review gate: direct service evidence creates exactly one confined sub-scope document and returns its exact target. No UI wiring.

[x] NDS-2 — Share The Interactive Create-To-Source Transition

  • [x] Add one reusable post-create coordinator that receives an already committed exact target.
  • [x] Update scope New, New Child, and New Sibling to refresh and establish their existing new-document selection before entering Source.
  • [x] Distinguish pre-commit failure from post-commit presentation failure and make recovery target-only.
  • [x] Preserve title-modal cancellation, busy-state, fixed source target, dirty-state, Save/Rebuild, Return, and route behavior.
  • [x] Add pure/module evidence for the transition order and failure split; avoid permanent tests of modal timing or focus choreography.

NDS-2 implementation and evidence

  • runInteractiveDocumentCreate invokes the create callback once, validates the returned committed target against the response identity, refreshes the owning projection, and only then requests Source with that exact target. Its create rejection branch recognizes only committed: true / retry_create: false service payloads and resumes from their target; presentation failures cannot return to the create callback.
  • Scope New, New Child, and New Sibling now share that coordinator. Their existing modal and placement rules are unchanged. Their existing reloadDocsIndex(<new-doc-id>) route/selection handoff completes before Source entry, and management busy state remains active until the editor mount accepts or fails.
  • Source entry resolves on the existing display-mode host's onAccepted callback rather than on request dispatch. Its new optional onFailed callback exposes asynchronous load/mount failure to management; management restores rendered mode while retaining the created document's route and selection. No public caller supplies the callback, so public mode behavior is unchanged.
  • Pre-commit errors render Create failed. Invalid committed responses, refresh failures, rejected Source requests, and asynchronous Source mount failures render Document created, but could not be opened in Source and retain the exact recoverable target when one was validated.
  • The focused create module smoke passed parent and sub-scope success, committed service-error recovery, ordinary pre-commit failure, refresh failure, Source rejection/failure, target mismatch, HTTP payload retention, exact Source context, rendered-mode recovery, and single create invocation. Existing router and Catalogue-token module smokes also passed.
  • Maintained explicit JavaScript lint over the three changed runtime files and Python lint/compilation over the new smoke and its profile registration: passed. Studio documentation and search dry-runs and git diff --check: passed.

Checkpoint / review gate: each existing interactive parent create action opens the correct new document in Source and cannot duplicate a committed create during recovery.

[x] NDS-3 — Add Report New

  • [x] Render New only in the manage report list, independent of selection and available when the collection is empty.
  • [x] Supply only the mounted { scope, sub_scope } collection to the create workflow.
  • [x] Refresh the manage inventory, establish the canonical subdoc route, and invoke the shared Source transition with the returned child target.
  • [x] Preserve unchanged public report imports, markup, controls, manifest, and by-ID payload contracts.
  • [x] Add focused contribution/report integration and local route evidence.
  • [x] Manually verify list placement, title modal, empty-list behavior, immediate editor state, Save/Rebuild return, Return without save, and post-commit recovery copy.

NDS-3 implementation and evidence

  • The manage contribution renders one collection-level New beside its selection-backed Actions control. It remains enabled for an empty report, blocks duplicate activation while one request is in flight, and passes only the mounted selection owner's exact { scope, sub_scope }. The report bridge revalidates both fields against its mounted parent/report configuration before calling management.
  • After a committed create, the shared report reloads its manage manifest with no-store, requires exactly one matching returned doc_id, publishes the refreshed inventory, writes the canonical subdoc route, and loads the exact by-ID detail with no-store before Source entry. Source retains report-session ownership so Save/Rebuild and Return project back to that detail without changing the selected parent.
  • The shared report still imports no management module. Its direct public module evidence retained zero contribution hosts and unchanged row, filter, status, manifest, and by-ID behavior; management supplies New only through the existing local contribution boundary.
  • Focused module smokes passed the empty-list button, selection independence, duplicate-click guard, exact collection bridge, first and subsequent refresh, no-store manifest/detail reads, canonical route, validated detail state, public separation, and the shared create-to-Source failure split. Existing router module evidence also passed.
  • A realistic manage-route smoke used an isolated temporary source tree and the real management service. It cancelled the ordinary title modal without a request, created the first and second flat child documents using exact { scope, title, sub_scope } bodies, opened each returned target immediately in Source, returned once without saving, and Save/Rebuilt the second into its exact rendered detail. It made no parent index/document reload during create.
  • The same route forced a rebuild failure after a third create had committed. The generated heading-only source remained present, the report made no second create or Source request, stayed rendered, and displayed Document created, but could not be opened in Source with the failed exact refresh detail.
  • The route confirmed both successful records in the manage manifest, public eligibility matching the configured scope default, and byte-identical parent Index, Recent, search, and Tag Registry sentinels. It created no repository document.
  • Manual inspection at 1440 × 1000 covered the empty list placement, ordinary title modal, immediate exact child source, Return detail, saved detail, and committed-create recovery copy. Narrow/mobile layout was not exercised in this phase.
  • Maintained explicit JavaScript lint over the seven changed runtime files, Python lint/compilation over the profile registration and two focused smokes, and git diff --check: passed. The broader profile, final generated consistency pass, and independent diff are recorded in NDS-4 below.

Checkpoint / review gate: one realistic sub-scope report can create its first and subsequent documents and lands directly in the existing editor.

[x] NDS-4 — Acceptance And Closeout

  • [x] Re-run the focused NDS-1 through NDS-3 evidence.
  • [x] Run maintained JavaScript/Python lint for changed source and the smallest relevant Docs Viewer smoke profile.
  • [x] Verify the new child source, manage inventory, canonical report route, public eligibility, and unchanged parent discovery outputs.
  • [x] Run Studio docs/search consistency and git diff --check.
  • [x] Record realistic manual UI acceptance and explicit omissions.
  • [x] Independently inspect the final diff before marking the delivery done.

NDS-4 acceptance evidence

  • Six focused service suites passed 76 current tests using a test-owned writable Projects base. They cover parent/child create, exact managed targets, metadata, sub-scope delete recovery, write/rebuild execution, and route dispatch. The earlier NDS-1 count was a point-in-time snapshot; the closeout records the named suites and their current collected count.
  • Focused create, report, route, router, and Catalogue-token smokes all passed. The route again covered exact create/Source requests, first and subsequent documents, Return, Save/Rebuild, committed-create recovery without a second write, manage/public eligibility, and unchanged parent/Tag Registry sentinels.
  • The maintained docs-viewer-smoke profile passed all 25/25 commands: repository-owned Docs Viewer lint, site validation, management/public module boundaries, and the relevant existing and new browser routes. Its run summary is var/admin/test-runs/new-document-source-entry-closeout/summary.md.
  • Manual inspection at 1440 × 1000 confirmed the compact 📄 report action, New title modal and wider title field, exact heading-only Source state, Return, saved rendered detail, and visible committed-create recovery copy.
  • No repository child document was created. Narrow/mobile layout, a live public write attempt, Tag Registry UI, and non-interactive creation workflows were not exercised because they remain outside this delivery.
  • Final review compared the pre-delivery base 530d84e5b through the working tree. Create uses only explicit validated targets/collections; the shared report imports no management module; no selected/displayed/URL/tag fallback was added. Two already-committed Analysis generated_at-only changes contain no Analysis record or content change.
  • Studio docs/search generation reported 230 documents, 13 tree roots, and zero warnings or pending generated writes. Full-delivery and working-tree git diff --check: passed.

Acceptance gate: the report and all existing interactive New actions open the exact committed document in Source, while public reports, non-interactive creation, Tag Registry workflows, and parent discovery remain unchanged.
